ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The cross section of a certain resistor made of a conducting medium is shown in the figure. The resistivity of the conducting medium is ρ, and it is made into the shape of a hemispherical shell layer with inner and outer radii a and b respectively (the shaded part in the figure). A spherical electrode with radius a and negligible resistance is embedded at the center of the sphere of the conducting medium to become one lead-out electrode, and a metal film with negligible resistance is plated on the outer spherical shell of the conducting medium to become another electrode. Let the resistance of this resistor be R. Among the following four expressions for R, only one is reasonable. You may not be able to solve for R, but you can judge the reasonableness of the following expressions through certain physical analysis. According to your judgment, the reasonable expression for R should be ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A conducting medium with resistivity ρ is made into a hemispherical shell layer with inner radius a and outer radius b. A spherical electrode with radius a and negligible resistance is embedded at the center of the sphere, and the outer surface is plated with a metal film with negligible resistance as another electrode. Let the resistance of this hemispherical shell be R; then what is the reasonable expression for R?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A conducting medium with resistivity ρ is made into a hemispherical shell layer with inner radius a and outer radius b. A spherical electrode with radius a and negligible resistance is embedded at the center of the sphere, and the outer surface is plated with a metal film with negligible resistance as another electrode. Let the resistance of this hemispherical shell be R; then what is the reasonable expression for R?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a cross-sectional schematic diagram. The gray shaded part is the hemispherical shell layer formed by the conducting medium; the center of the sphere is marked as O, there is a low-resistance spherical electrode at the center with radius marked as a, and it is connected to an upper lead wire. An arrow in the figure marks the current I; the radius of the outer hemispherical surface is marked as b, and the outer surface has a metal film and is connected to a lower lead wire. As can be seen from the figure, the conducting medium occupies only the hemispherical shell region, so the current from the inner spherical surface to the outer hemispherical surface can spread in the radial direction. Reasoning: Since the inner spherical electrode and the outer-surface metal film have negligible resistance, they can be regarded as equipotential surfaces; the hemispherical shell has radial symmetry about the center of the sphere, so take a thin hemispherical shell with radius r and thickness dr as a series element. The conducting cross-sectional area of this element perpendicular to the current direction is the hemispherical area 2πr^2, so the element resistance dR = ρ dr/(2πr^2). Integrating these elements in series from r=a to r=b: R = ∫_a^b ρ dr/(2πr^2) = ρ/(2π)(1/a - 1/b) = ρ(b-a)/(2πab).
